title: Euler's theorem: existence of Eulerian trails (Hierholzer, formalize-only)
why_not_classical: Euler 1736 / Hierholzer 1873: a finite connected graph has an Eulerian circuit iff every degree is even, and an Eulerian trail iff exactly 0 or 2 vertices have odd degree. Completely settled. Value is a Mathlib contribution (Trails.lean has IsEulerian + the necessary parity; ProofLab now has circuit + 2-odd trail existence). Archive Konigsberg is a negative instance on a custom graph, not this theorem. Do NOT re-fund as novel.

statement_pin_required.convention: Fix G : SimpleGraph V, Fintype V, G.Connected. Let oddDeg = {v | Odd (G.degree v)}. TRAIL CLAUSE ONLY: card oddDeg = 2 → ∃ u ≠ v odd-degree with an Eulerian Walk u v. Use Mathlib Walk.IsEulerian. Encoding: Hierholzer / longest trail from an odd-degree start. Do NOT dummy-edge.
landmines: Connectedness is essential. Do not copy the Trails.lean TODO without G.Connected.
Do NOT dummy-edge: SimpleGraph has no parallel edges and cannot add an edge that already exists (the OPE-597 failure mode when the two odd vertices are already adjacent).
SimpleGraph has no parallel edges; do not formalize Königsberg.
Eulerian ≠ Hamiltonian. Do not re-prime Dirac.
Do NOT re-prime Level A K_1 / C_n / K_2.
Do NOT re-prime Level B circuit clause / eulerian_complete_odd / nonempty-edgeSet circuit.
